correctness.rationale: For every integer \(N\ge4\) and \(1<t<2\), a dual potential is extreme precisely when its tight-edge graph is connected. With no long tight edge, integrality and the strict diameter bound force binary values, whose exhaustive distinguished-pair table contributes \(8\cdot2^{N-3}-10\) potentials. With a long tight edge, regular coordinates take precisely two possible levels and distinguished coordinates fit three signed positive patterns and their negatives, contributing \(6\cdot2^{N-3}\) potentials. Their total is \(7\cdot2^{N-2}-10\). Separate endpoint classifications establish \(2^N-2\) at \(t=1\) and \(2^N-4\) at \(t=2\). Polarity identifies dual vertices with primal facets. The provided exact checker exhaustively enumerated small cases \(N=4,5,6\) and \(t=1,3/2,2\), passing all nine. The universal conclusion rests on the proof, not those finite cases.

originality.rationale: The new all-N exact interior facet law and its full extremal-potential classification concern a non-transitive, two-edge path of elongated distances. Published results on the generic Lipschitz polytope, complete-multipartite snowflakes, disjoint shortened pairs and dense symmetric-edge inball contacts either use different assumptions or answer different invariants. Full relevant primary text and published exact-neighbor claims were inspected. There is residual risk of unindexed equivalent specialized enumerations, but no identified source presently implies the interior count.
residual_risks: Unindexed specialized finite metric or transportation-polytope facet tables may contain an equivalent closed form.
A future broader arbitrary long-edge graph enumeration could subsume this simple path case.
The endpoint t=2 graph metric has general known tools and is included for contrast rather than asserted new independently.

value.rationale: A path of two incident stretched pairs is the smallest natural non-cluster long-edge pattern; it cannot be reduced to the previously known partition or shortened-matching enumerations. The result supplies a complete closed all-dimension facet invariant and the full dual extremizer classification, with a strict interior surplus and two discontinuous endpoint changes. The \(7/4\) limiting facet ratio reflects a nonadditive local-defect interaction useful for understanding stability of metric polytope combinatorics. No arbitrary slices, trivial sign test, or unsupported downstream theorem is needed for this exact natural classification.
